Confirms it: `calibration_eligible` is only produced by `nfl-auto-picks.js` (the live/production path), never by `nfl-replay.js`'s raw candidates (which is what `nfl-blind-audit.js` feeds through). Field is `undefined` there, moot anyway since the flag is `false`.

## Findings

**1. minEdge:3 was never calibrated to predict outcomes.** The only place edge-magnitude vs. outcome is even examined is the *separate, unwired* diagnostic in `server/services/nfl-candidate-analysis.js:41-49` (`edgeCalibration`), whose 3.0–3.9 bucket is explicitly the minEdge:3 boundary. That function's own findings (lines 228-236) say the weak-edge bucket can be net-negative ROI and the edge-ranking `state` can read `'broken'`. Every call site of this report (`nfl-candidate-analysis.js:276-277,286-291`) is labeled `warning: 'Post-hoc selectivity diagnostic. Thresholds are not promotion rules...'`. Nothing feeds this back into `nfl-policy.js`. `minEdge: 3` (nfl-policy.js:21) is a hardcoded literal with no citation to any backtest that validated 3 points specifically.

**2. requireCalibratedAdvantage:false disables the only calibration gate that exists.** `nfl-policy.js:198-200`: when true, a candidate is abstained unless `candidate.calibration_eligible === true`; when false (as in `NFL_HISTORICAL_REPLAY_POLICY`, nfl-policy.js:91), this check is skipped entirely — confirmed by grep, `calibration_eligible` is only ever populated in the live path (`nfl-auto-picks.js:180`), never by `nfl-replay.js`'s raw candidates that feed `nfl-blind-audit.js`. Setting it false doesn't just no-op — it also silently drops the EV floor: `NFL_HISTORICAL_REPLAY_POLICY.minExpectedReturn: null` (nfl-policy.js:98) disables the `expected_return < minExpectedReturn` abstention (nfl-policy.js:237-241) too, per that policy's own comment: "that selector had no executable-return gate."

**3. maxDisagreement:4.5 only clips magnitude, never validates direction.** `applyNflPolicy` (nfl-policy.js:203-205) abstains only when `disagreement > maxDisagreement` — a ceiling on how far raw can differ from market, with no corresponding check that the *sign* of the edge is trustworthy. The one analysis that tests whether disagreement carries directional signal is `aggregate()`'s component-agreement split in `nfl-blind-audit.js:434-438,485-496` — and it found z=0.84 (not significant) / "not demonstrably carrying information, filtering on it would be fitting noise" (line 495-496). That split is a post-run reporting artifact, not a gate `applyNflPolicy` reads.

**4. Bottom line: no, raw mode has no kill-switch.** `market_residual` mode is blocked by `residual_gate_passed` (0/848 fits) before it ever reaches the policy layer. `raw` mode has no analogous circuit breaker: `requireCalibratedAdvantage=false` and `minExpectedReturn=null` remove both checks that could catch "this edge isn't real," and `minEdge`/`maxDisagreement` are fixed, uncalibrated numeric filters that always fire picks as long as any candidate happens to clear them — regardless of whether raw's current edge signal is known-good or known-broken that week.

Confirmed: `fitEnsemble`'s scoring loop at line 1527 does `MODELS.map(...)` unconditionally — the full static array, every call, no history-based filtering except the static `challengerOnly` flag and a caller-supplied `excluded` set (line 1791, used for family-contract diagnostics, not automatic).

---

**1. Components (server/services/nfl-ensemble.js:642-933) and redundancy groups**

22 always-active + 9 `challengerOnly` (never weighted unless the caller explicitly sets `includeChallengers`, L1624): availability, roster_strength*, massey, colley, pythagorean, point_diff, melo, dynamic_state, epa_net, epa_neutral, early_down_eff*, pass_eff_matchup*, rush_eff_matchup*, explosive_pass*, pressure_response*, series_sustain*, field_position*, second_half_eff*, success_rate, explosive, drive_eff, situational, trenches, turnover_regressed, opp_adjusted, recent_form, rest_travel, pace_total, weather_total, market_anchor, market_regression (*=challenger).

Redundant groups beyond market_anchor/market_regression, judged from each `predict`:
- **Rating-system cluster (massey L674, point_diff L697, melo L705):** all three reduce to "season-long scoring-margin rating differenced + hfa" — Massey least-squares, raw margin/game, and Elo built to track margin are near-linear transforms of the same underlying signal (colley L679 is the one genuine outlier since it drops margin entirely).
- **EPA-net cluster (epa_net L723, epa_neutral L728, opp_adjusted L817):** all compute `net_epa`-style off-minus-def differentials from the same `c.feat`/`c.agg` team splits; opp_adjusted's own note (L818-823) admits it previously *algebraically equaled* epa_net and even post-fix is "the plain net-EPA component it replaces functionally," unvalidated against it.
- **Explosiveness pair (explosive L781, explosive_pass L751):** big-play rate overall vs. passing-only big-play rate — same underlying feature, narrower slice.
- **Down/situation cluster (early_down_eff L736, situational L791, series_sustain L761):** all reduce to "does this offense sustain drives / convert downs," differing only in which down-window they slice.
- **turnover_regressed (L803)** overlaps point_diff/massey (same `pf-pa` margin base, turnover term faded not removed).

**2. No pruning/retirement mechanism exists.** `challengerOnly` (e.g. L663, L736) only *gates new, unproven* signals out of production weight until some human edits the flag — there is no code path that ever sets it (grep for `challengerOnly =` finds only comparisons, never an assignment) and no promotion/graduation code exists (searched `promot|graduat`; the one hit at L315 explicitly says promotion "belongs to the promotion gate in staking.js" — a different, market-residual-only gate, not a per-component registry). There is likewise no demotion path for an established (non-challenger) component that turns out useless — no enabled/disabled registry, no deprecation list.

**3. Confirmed: every call re-evaluates the full static list.** `fitEnsemble`'s `scored = MODELS.map(m => {...})` (L1527) and the weighting loop (L1619-1634) iterate the entire hardcoded `MODELS` array every invocation. A chronically bad non-challenger component never gets excluded — only down-weighted via `Math.exp(-0.7 * rmse)` (L1628), which is always >0. So it keeps contributing nonzero, potentially correlated, dilution every week indefinitely, with no code-level mechanism to stop that short of a human deleting/flagging it in source.

Read the target reports directly (all confirmed present in repo root / docs/). Findings below are distinct from the known 0/848 promotion-gate and the exp(-0.7·RMSE) ensemble-weight bug.

**Ranked, documented-but-unfixed issues:**

1. **Margin-model calibration gate currently blocks 100% of models — zero edge computable this week.** `NEWS_TIMING_REPORT.md`: tracing a real Tua Tagovailoa injury (~1pt real market move) through to today's ATL@PIT decision yields **0.0 edge points**, "because 0 of 31 margin models are currently calibration-eligible (fresh gate from yesterday's model merge)." Distinct from the 848-artifact residual gate — this is the per-margin-model calibration gate, and it's presently wide open (blocking everyone), not a statistical non-result.

2. **Order-book depth data has been silently discarded since 2026-08-29, unrecoverable.** `MODEL_BUILD_REPORT.md`: `captureOrderBooks()` fetches the full ladder but persists only the top-of-book touch, so realistic fill/execution backtesting is structurally impossible on history ("no backfill can fix it — the data was never written"). The fix (migration 044 + best-first capture) is written but explicitly **"file only, not applied"** as of the report — every half hour unapplied is more unrecoverable data loss.

3. **T-60 news packet's source table is 5 days stale.** `NEWS_TIMING_REPORT.md`: `nfl_news_events` "is 5 days stale and never saw this specific fact," independently verified against the live DB — a second, separate reason (alongside #1) that a real, verified injury fact produced zero effect on a live decision.

4. **Reintroduced cross-game injury leak, patched but unverified.** `GIANT_PLAN_BUILD_REPORT.md` §2.2: pipeline stage 6 swapped the injury read to `nfl_feature_revisions`, whose entity key carries no team — "the replacement re-introduced the identical cross-game leak" that an earlier fix had closed. The merge-synthesized LEFT JOIN fix is untested: "no test in the repo exercises team-scoping of this specific bitemporal path," flagged as "the single highest-synthesis-risk line in this entire merge."

5. **Pre-existing `resolveQuoteBasis` date-boundary bug, unfixed across 6 branches.** `GIANT_PLAN_BUILD_REPORT.md`/`BETTING_INSANE_REPORT.md`: same failing test confirmed present on unmodified main by six independent branches; "has never actually been fixed by anyone."

6. **Explicitly small samples flagged as inconclusive, not padded as evidence.** `NEWS_TIMING_REPORT.md` (n=1–12 at tightest reaction windows, "11 days of one preseason-into-week-1 stretch"); `BETTING_INSANE_REPORT.md` (props-to-spread walk-forward: 9 cutoffs vs. a full 54-cutoff sweep, "a larger sample would be worth running before treating it as fully conclusive").

**1. Intended purpose** — `server/services/nfl-signal-reliability.js:1-8`: a "cutoff-safe reliability controller" that can only *shrink* (never boost) a component's ensemble weight, and only after "enough frozen, independently settled forward examples show directional harm and worse squared error than the market." Explicitly scoped: "candidate forecast influence only; production and staking authority unchanged" (`:130`).

**2. Firing condition** — `deriveSignalReliability` (`:31-81`): needs `overall.n >= MIN_EXAMPLES(32)` and `weeks >= MIN_WEEKS(4)` (`:13-14,60`) just to leave `'warming'` state. Then either (a) `strong_harm`: 90%-Wilson-upper directional rate `<0.5` AND MSE-gain `<0` → multiplier 0.25 (`:61-62`), or (b) `probable_harm`: directional rate `<0.47` AND MSE-gain `<0` AND recent evidence not contradictory → multiplier 0.6 (`:63-66`).

**3. Structurally unreachable right now, with direct evidence.** Production picks never even query it: `nfl-ensemble.js:1729-1730` — when `includeChallengers` is false (the real-pick path), `reliability = {version:'production-unchanged', multipliers:{}}` is hardcoded, bypassing `signalReliabilityFor` entirely. That's *by design* (`reliability_controller.mode: 'off'` for production, `:1858`), so every real audit trace showing `multiplier=1, adjusted=false` is expected, not a bug in itself.
But even for candidate/shadow evaluation, it has never fired: `nfl_signal_reliability_artifacts` has **0 rows** (queried live DB, read-only). `buildSignalReliabilityArtifact` is only invoked from `nfl-model-growth.js:211-212`, gated on `afterIngest.finalized_week > 0`. Every one of the 40 recorded growth runs shows `finalized_week=0, status='waiting'` (queried `nfl_model_growth_runs`) — the season-2026 growth cycle has never reached that line. And `shadow_decisions` (the only data source, `nfl-signal-reliability.js:85-116`) has only **8** settled NFL-spread rows across **2** distinct weeks — far below `MIN_EXAMPLES=32` / `MIN_WEEKS=4` even if the artifact were built. With `signalReliabilityFor` falling back to `'neutral-cold-start'` (`:149`) whenever no artifact exists, the multiplier map is always `{}`.

**4. Yes — this plausibly matters, but isn't the current bottleneck.** For it to help: (a) production would need to actually consume it (currently structurally excluded), and (b) the shadow pipeline needs ≥4 weeks and ≥32 independent settled examples per component — implying the mechanism can't even theoretically activate until well into the season. Its absence means a chronically-harmful component (if one exists) is never downweighted in real picks — consistent with the earlier-found dead promotion gate, this is a second safety mechanism that is live in code but inert in practice, this time because production intentionally never wires to it and the shadow data volume hasn't reached its own threshold.

Yes — three more real, distinct issues, plus two smaller ones worth flagging. None of these are the promotion gate or the RMSE-weighting bug; they're separate holes.

**1. The path actually generating your live picks (raw mode) has no quality gate at all.**
Since residual has never promoted, every real pick runs through `raw` mode — and `NFL_HISTORICAL_REPLAY_POLICY` sets `requireCalibratedAdvantage:false` and `minExpectedReturn:null` (nfl-policy.js:91,98), which switches off the only two checks that could catch "this edge isn't real." What's left — `minEdge:3` and `maxDisagreement:4.5` — are fixed numbers never validated against outcomes (the one diagnostic that checks this, in nfl-candidate-analysis.js, is explicitly labeled "not promotion rules" and shows the weak-edge bucket can be net-negative). **Class: can't detect its own bad picks.** This is probably the biggest one — it's the mode that's actually live.

**2. The one mechanism built to auto-shrink a harmful component has never fired, and structurally can't yet.**
`nfl-signal-reliability.js` is designed to downweight a component once it shows real, settled harm — but production hardcodes it off for real picks (nfl-ensemble.js:1729-1730), and even in shadow evaluation it has zero artifacts: the growth pipeline that would build them is stuck at `finalized_week=0`, and the underlying data has only 8 settled rows across 2 weeks against a required 32 examples / 4 weeks. **Class: can't detect its own bad picks.** A second safety net, separately dead from the promotion gate.

**3. No component ever gets pruned — only down-weighted.**
`fitEnsemble` scores the full static 22-component list every run (nfl-ensemble.js:1527) with no retirement path. Several clusters are near-duplicates of each other (massey/point_diff/melo; epa_net/epa_neutral/opp_adjusted; the two explosiveness rate signals), and a permanently bad or redundant one can only be shrunk via the RMSE formula — never excluded. **Class: diluted signal.** Even after the joint-regression fix lands, correlated noise stays in the blend indefinitely.

Worth a shorter mention, lower priority: a cross-game injury-data leak was reintroduced and patched with zero test coverage on that exact path (flagged as the highest-risk line in the recent merge), and a `resolveQuoteBasis` date-boundary bug has gone unfixed across six branches. Both are real, both are "corrupted/stale input" problems rather than modeling ones. I'm discounting the order-book-data-loss and this-week's-calibration-gate items — real, but about execution backtesting and a transient state, not why picks aren't improving.

**Bottom line:** the raw-weighting fix is necessary but not sufficient — it doesn't touch #1 or #2, so even a correctly-weighted blend is still running with no live quality gate and no working harm-detection, which will keep capping how good production picks can actually get.
